heading_sections.title: Seedream 5.5 Prompt Guide: 10 Prompts That Work (With Results)
text: Ten Seedream 5.5 prompts with the real image each one produced: signs, posters, portraits, products, food, rooms, anime and more, plus three photo edit prompts.
VdoBloom Team
November 10, 2026

Seedream 5.5 works best with a full sentence that names the subject, the place, the light and the framing, with any words you want in the picture inside quotes. Below are ten prompts we ran on 10 November 2026, each with the first image it produced, the shape and the credit cost, plus three edit prompts on one photo. Copy any of them into the AI image generator and pick Seedream 5.5.
Every image on this page is a first take from Seedream 5.5 on VdoBloom, not edited.

heading_sections.title: What is Seedream 5.5?
text: Seedream 5.5 is the image generation and editing model from ByteDance Seed , the team behind the Seedream series. It was introduced on November 9, 2026 as the next step after Seedream 5.0 Pro , with three headline upgrades: more stable multi-turn editing, native RGBA output with transparent backgrounds, and more realistic images with clearer text.

In ByteDance's announcement , the model keeps unedited areas unchanged at the pixel level, shown over 100 rounds of edits on one image. It renders skin, light and materials with less gloss and overexposure, and handles dense small text in English and Chinese with fewer errors. ByteDance reports better quality and usability scores than 5.0 Pro in all six use cases it tested, and a lead over GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst and Nano Banana 2.1 on text structure and text-to-image realism in its own tests.

On Flux1 AI you use it in the browser, with no BytePlus account or API key, on the same credits as 40+ other models. Most runs finish in under 40 seconds, much faster than 5.0 Pro here. For quick drafts, Seedream 5.0 Flash is still the cheapest Seedream.

heading_sections.title: Seedream 5.5 features
text: The three upgrades ByteDance announced, plus what we saw in our own runs.

heading_sections.title: Photos that look photographed
text: ByteDance says 5.5 renders light, materials and skin more naturally, with less of the glossy, overexposed look AI images often have. In our portrait test, fine lines, loose hair in the backlight and a matte mug all read as a real photo.

heading_sections.title: Small text you can read
text: Dense captions, numbered steps and complex Chinese characters come out cleaner. ByteDance measured a 0.4% severe text error rate. Our coffee infographic got all six steps right, including temperatures and grams.

heading_sections.title: Transparent PNGs, built in
text: Set Background to Transparent and the model draws the alpha channel itself, including see-through glass and soft fur edges. The PNG drops straight onto a slide, product page or design file, with no background removal step.

heading_sections.title: Edits that leave the rest alone
text: Upload up to 10 images and say what should change. ByteDance trained 5.5 to keep unedited areas pixel-identical, so you can reuse a result as the next reference and keep refining without the picture drifting.

heading_sections.title: Standard or transparent background?
text: Both settings cost the same. The Background setting only decides what fills the space around your subject.

heading_sections.title: Good to know before you start
text: Honest notes on what this workflow does and does not do.

heading_sections.title: 2K is the maximum here
text: Our provider serves this model at up to 2K, so there is no 3K or 4K on this page. For 4K, use Nano Banana 2.1 or GPT Image 2.5 .

heading_sections.title: References are charged
text: Each uploaded image adds 1 credit, including the first one, because our provider bills every reference. A plain text-to-image run has no extra charge.

heading_sections.title: One image per run
text: Each run returns a single image. For a series, run again with the same prompt, or reuse your best result as a reference to keep the look.

heading_sections.title: No layers or Pro version yet
text: Some sites list layer splitting or 4K for this model. We do not offer them, and ByteDance says a Pro version of 5.5 will follow later. For a cut-out of an existing photo, our free background remover also works.

heading_sections.title: Prompts are rewritten upstream
text: The provider runs prompt optimization on every request, and we cannot turn it off. Very literal prompts may gain small extras, such as a seal stamp on a Chinese poster. Write "No other text" when the layout is fixed.

heading_sections.title: Content rules apply
text: Explicit or NSFW content is not supported. Prompts and uploads are screened, ByteDance's safeguards also check them, and a blocked run is refunded. Proofread any text before you publish it.

heading_sections.title: Is Seedream 5.5 free to use?
text: Each image costs 6 credits at 1.5K or 10 at 2K, plus 1 per reference image. Credits come with any Flux1 AI plan and work on every model here. No BytePlus account is needed, and failed runs are refunded.

heading_sections.title: When was Seedream 5.5 released?
text: ByteDance Seed introduced it on November 9, 2026. It follows Seedream 5.0 Pro , released in July 2026, and is available on Flux1 AI now.

heading_sections.title: Is there a Seedream 5.5 Pro?
text: Not yet. ByteDance's announcement says a Pro version of the 5.5 series will follow. Until then, the model on this page is the newest Seedream.

heading_sections.title: Seedream 5.5 vs Seedream 5.0 Pro: what changed?
text: ByteDance lists steadier multi-turn edits, native transparent backgrounds, more realistic images and clearer small text. On this site, 5.5 costs the same per image, finishes in seconds instead of minutes, and bills every reference, while 5.0 Pro includes the first one free.

heading_sections.title: Can Seedream 5.5 make transparent PNGs?
text: Yes. Set Background to Transparent and you get a PNG with a real alpha channel, including partial transparency for glass, hair and soft edges. It works from a prompt or from an uploaded photo you want cut out, at no extra cost.

heading_sections.title: Is there a Seedream 5.5 API?
text: ByteDance offers Seedream through its BytePlus platforms; check there for official 5.5 API access and pricing. The Flux1 AI API does not serve 5.5 yet, but it does serve Seedream 5.0 Pro and 5.0 Flash; see the API docs . This page needs no API key.

heading_sections.title: Can I download Seedream 5.5 and run it locally?
text: No. Seedream is a closed ByteDance model with no public weights, so it only runs through ByteDance's services and platforms built on them. Everything you generate here downloads as a PNG.

heading_sections.title: How to use Seedream 5.5 on Froging AI
Start with a clear brief
text: For a new image, specify the subject, framing, and light. For a photo edit, upload the approved reference and describe one visible change. Name what should carry through, such as the product position, texture, and direction of the shadow.

heading_sections.title: Choose the frame and output
text: Use 1:1 for a square campaign image, 16:9 for a wide banner, or Original to keep the source shape during an edit. Try 1K for a first pass and 2K when the final placement needs more detail. Choose Transparent when the image will sit over another design.

heading_sections.title: Review, revise, and download
text: Compare the new image with the original at the size people will see. Check any small text separately at full size. Save the approved PNG before trying the next edit so each round has a clear reference.

heading_sections.title: Keep control across several edits
text: For a product shoot with several revisions, start with the broadest change, such as the backdrop. Use the approved result as the reference for smaller changes to props or reflections. This makes it easier to see which request changed the details you wanted to keep.

Check geometry and color separately. A new surface can change the perceived color of a white object even when the silhouette stays in place. For a catalog, compare the result with a known color reference and check fine print before publishing.

heading_sections.title: Prepare transparent graphics for real layouts
text: Transparent output works for stickers, product cutouts, and decorative elements that need to move between layouts. Describe the edges, material, and whether you want a shadow. For a reusable cutout, leave room around the object so thin details stay inside the canvas.
Test the downloaded PNG on both a light and a dark background. A faint fringe can blend into one layout and stand out in another, particularly around glass, hair, and reflective surfaces.

heading_sections.title: What is Seedream 5.5? add
text: Seedream 5.5 is ByteDance's newest Seedream image model and the default model in Seedream Studio. It makes images from a text prompt and edits images you give it, with up to 10 references, in eight aspect ratios and up to 4K.

heading_sections.title: Can I use Seedream 5.5 free online? add
text: Yes. Seedream 5.5 runs in your browser in Seedream Studio, and new accounts get 75 free credits with no credit card. A Standard image costs 75 credits and a High image costs 100 credits.

heading_sections.title: Does Seedream 5.5 make 4K images? add
text: Yes, at the High tier: 3840 × 2160 for 16:9 and 2160 × 3840 for 9:16. High sizes in the other aspect ratios have about the same number of pixels, so the largest square is 2880 × 2880.

heading_sections.title: How do I get a transparent background? add
text: Choose Seedream 5.5 and turn on the Transparent background switch before you generate. It works for text-to-image, edits and batch runs, at no extra cost. Transparent results come back as PNG files, and opaque results as JPEG.

heading_sections.title: Can I keep editing the same image? add
text: Yes. Use a result as the reference for your next edit, as in the three rounds above. ByteDance says Seedream 5.5 keeps its quality through more than 80 rounds of edits; this page shows three.

heading_sections.title: How many reference images can I use? add
text: Up to 10 in one edit. The result takes the aspect ratio and size you choose, not the shape of your reference images.

heading_sections.title: Can I choose a custom size? add
text: Not on Seedream 5.5: it offers 16 preset sizes, eight Standard and eight High. Seedream 5 Pro takes custom sizes.

heading_sections.title: Is Seedream 5 Pro still available? add
text: Yes. Seedream 5 Pro, with Flash Fast and custom sizes, and Seedream 5 Lite stay in the model picker. Seedream 5.5 is the default for new sessions.

heading_sections.title: Seedream 5.5 User Guide: 100 Rounds of Edits on One Image, With Untouched Areas Preserved Pixel for Pixel
text: ByteDance has released Seedream 5.5, an image creation model with steadier multi-round editing that can also generate transparent assets directly. The accompanying user guide gives sets of prompts and results by use case, so you can copy them and get started.

ByteDance's Seed team has released Seedream 5.5, its new image creation model. The official bar is practical: for an image model to enter a professional team's real workflow, it has to keep producing usable results under constraints of delivery standards, time and cost. This release makes three upgrades toward that goal:

In the official evaluation, senior reviewers scored results across six scenarios: e-commerce, marketing, film and TV, games, office work and fashion design. Compared with the previous generation, Seedream 5.0 Pro, quality scores and usability rates rose in all six, and usability for film/TV and office work more than doubled. On text, the share of images with severe garbled, missing or malformed text fell to 0.4%, and minor problems to 1.7%. Against GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst and Nano Banana 2.1, ByteDance says Seedream 5.5 leads on text structure and on text-to-image realism. The model is rolling out on Jimeng (Dreamina), Doubao, Doubao Work and Volcano Ark.

Jimeng shipped a user guide with the model. It first covers four capabilities, each with a one-line prompt pattern; then lays out sets of “prompt + generated result” across 5 personal-use categories and 7 commercial scenarios; and ends with two word lists (style words and aesthetic words) and 9 tips for writing prompts.

What makes the guide worth a close read is that it demonstrates a new way of working: generate one image, then refine it round by round. Editing AI images used to feel like gambling: change one thing and something else changed too, so people got used to writing everything in one sentence and regenerating the whole image if it was off. The three upgrades in 5.5, plus the line that keeps recurring in the guide, “keep everything else unchanged,” all turn image generation into revision. Below we walk through the guide in its own order. Every example image is included, and the prompts follow the guide (translated into English where the original was Chinese), so you can copy them. The examples were all picked by ByteDance, so your own results will vary.
Counted by the guide's chapters: each example set is one prompt with its generated result; a demo video counts as one set.

heading_sections.title: 100 rounds on one image, with untouched areas left alone
text: Anyone who has edited images with AI has probably run into this: ask it to change a cup's color and the face quietly shifts a little; do another round and the background gets a bit blurrier. ByteDance's blog explains why: each round's output becomes the next round's input, so tiny deviations accumulate with every edit and end up as lost detail and degraded quality.

The figure below actually runs that process. It is the same small pixel image, and each round the little snake moves one cell to the right. On the left, every round redraws the whole image, and every pixel picks up a slight error; on the right, only the snake's cells change and every other pixel is copied as-is.

Illustration: The per-round error on the left is a magnitude we picked for the demo and does not represent any real model's measurements. It illustrates the principle: a small drift per round becomes obvious after 100 rounds, while on the right, “pixels you did not name are not touched at all” is what ByteDance calls pixel-level preservation of non-edited regions.

Seedream 5.5 got dedicated training for this. In the official demo, one work was edited for 100 consecutive rounds, each building on the previous result. After many rounds of swapping clothes, accessories and objects on the table, it can still make fine edits to small things like a ring or glasses frames, and the contact, occlusion and lighting between accessories and skin still line up.
Official demo: 100 consecutive edits on one work, each round building on the previous result.
Another clip from the same demo in the guide (man playing chess): each round gets just one edit instruction, and the number in the corner of the frame jumps through 021, 058, 084, 098.

heading_sections.title: Generate transparent images directly, no more cutouts
text: Anyone who does design knows how annoying cutouts are: hair strands, feathers and glass always leave a ring of stray color at the edge. Seedream 5.5 takes a different approach: while generating, it works out “where is empty” too, and hands you an image with a transparent background directly.

Each pixel in an ordinary image stores three numbers: red, green and blue (RGB). A transparent image stores one more, called A (alpha, opacity): 0 is fully transparent, 255 is fully opaque, and numbers in between are semi-transparent. RGBA means these four numbers. The sticker below is drawn live on this page; wherever the white line sweeps, the A value of every pixel in that row is read out.

Illustration: We drew the sticker. It works on any background without another cutout, because every pixel carries its own opacity; the edge and the glass bead have A values between 0 and 255, so they blend naturally onto whatever sits behind them.

ByteDance describes this capability as outputting transparent or semi-transparent images with an alpha channel directly, with careful handling of outlines and transparent regions. In the demo, a snowy owl with spread wings keeps the feather tips on its wings, the tiny gaps between feathers, and the outline of its talons. The official material adds one caveat: transparent materials like glass are not the same as a transparent background, so you have to write in the prompt which parts are semi-transparent and which should be cut out.
The same stickers on several background colors still work.

heading_sections.title: Photos that look more like real photographs
text: AI images give themselves away by being too perfect: oily skin, blown-out highlights, light that is bright everywhere. This release improves lighting, materials and skin texture in realistic scenes, reducing the over-shiny, over-exposed and blotchy look. The guide breaks it into four points: natural composition, better skin texture, believable expressions and poses, and harmonious light and shadow.
Four examples from the guide's “realistic texture” section: someone blocking a corner of the lens, the harshness of direct flash, dust and fallen leaves in backlight, all like a casually taken photo.

Examples from the official blog. Top: the highlight-to-shadow transition on the girl's shoulder and stray hair in backlight; soft window light on the father's arm. heading_sections.title: Small text and many-stroke characters, rendered more accurately
text: Posters, infographics and product labels are most vulnerable to typos. This release improves the generation and layout of dense small text, and many-stroke Chinese characters stay legible at small sizes. The guide's key points: accurate text in complex scenes, clear small text, sound structure, and better canvas layout and color.

Four examples from the guide's “text structure” section: a conference long poster, a Song-dynasty tea infographic, an English poster, and a game design page. All the small text was generated directly by the model.

Two examples from the official blog. Top: a blue morpho diagram with eight image-and-text groups on antennae, wing veins and scales; the Chinese notes next to the magnified details are very small. Bottom: a Shakespeare-themed newspaper layout, with paragraphs of small English text between portraits and illustrations.

ByteDance measures this with a “text corruption rate”: the share of generated images with wrong characters, missing characters or broken structure. The test covers Chinese and English and dense small text.

Data comes from the official blog's evaluation chart; both groups are drawn on the same scale. Severe corruption fell from 2.8% in the previous generation to 0.4%; minor corruption from 2.6% to 1.7%. The evaluation was run by ByteDance.

A low rate does not mean it never errs. In the UI section of the guide, the landmark icon set got 5 of 6 English place names wrong, for example labeling the Oriental Pearl Tower “NEW YORKA.” For text that matters, spell it out character by character using the pattern below.

heading_sections.title: Official evaluation: against the previous generation and against rivals
text: Besides text corruption rate, ByteDance ran two more evaluations. The first looks at usability rate and average subjective score across six production scenarios, compared only with the previous generation.

Official evaluation chart. Left: Usability Rate; right: mean opinion score (MOS). The six directions are e-commerce, marketing, film and TV, games, office work and fashion design, with the overall at the top. The dark line is 5.5 and the light line is 5.0 Pro; in Film & TV and Office Productivity, 5.5's usability rate is more than double the previous version's. Reading off the scale, 5.5's overall usability is about 20% (about 10% for the previous version), and the highest, film and TV, is about 30%.
The second looks at text structure and realism: reviewers compare two models' outputs and pick the better one, scored with GSB (Good/Same/Bad). A positive value means reviewers favored Seedream 5.5.

Data comes from the official blog's evaluation chart. One of the twelve comparisons is negative: on the image-to-image realism task, reviewers preferred Nano Banana 2.1 (−6.18%). That is why ByteDance's conclusion says it leads on “text structure and text-to-image realism.” Against the previous generation all four are positive, with image-to-image realism highest at +55.62%.

heading_sections.title: What Makes a Good Seedream 5.5 Prompt?
text: A useful prompt separates the subject, visual treatment, and constraints. For a new image, describe the scene and composition. For an edit, identify the exact change, then name the features that must remain consistent.

ByteDance's Seedream 5.5 model page highlights multi-turn editing, transparent assets, and image creation. The prompts below turn those directions into practical briefs, while leaving room to inspect the actual output.
Use this structure as a starting point:

Create or edit [subject]. Use [scene and composition], [lighting], and [materials or style]. Change [specific element]. Preserve [important details]. Include [exact text or export requirement], if needed.

You don't need every part in every prompt. A portrait doesn't need a paragraph about typography, and a packaging color change doesn't need a new camera setup. Include the details that help the model make the right decision.

heading_sections.title: What we liked and what held it back
What the images look like
text: The gallery contains eight published examples from the model page. Everything shown is publishable. Our content-test images are not displayed; those results are reported in words.

Lettering. KAZE RAMEN reproduced the English title, Japanese subtitle, four item lines and opening-hours footnote letter for letter. It also added Japanese lettering at the side; that prompt did not prohibit extra words. NOIR's prompt ruled out any extra text, and the cover kept to the masthead, Japanese line, issue line and barcode.
Cutout. The teal fox mug is a product cutout with a real alpha channel. The 2k PNG separates the mug cleanly from its background.
Light and people. The jazz-bar image shows two women slow dancing in a dim bar under warm amber light.
Edits. The rainy Tokyo edit changed the outfit and location from one portrait while keeping the face. The rooftop edit used two portraits, named by image number, and kept both people recognisable.

Layers. NOIR returned six images at a ceiling of six: background, person, masthead, Japanese line, issue line and barcode. KAZE also returned six at six. These examples show separated design elements, while the four-image poster result shows why the cap is not a promised count.

heading_sections.title: How far it goes
text: SpicyAPI adds no content filter. On 7 November 2026, we ran 56 requests across three endpoints: 18 text to image, 18 edits and 20 layer splits. The test covered five levels from Mild to Maximum, used adult subjects only and included a visual check of every image. No request was refused. We publish the levels, but not the test prompts.
Maximum had six runs per endpoint because we used two probe types. All 20 layer runs split correctly.

Reading the table. Text to image delivered every level in every run. Edits delivered every level, with one toned-down run each at Strong and Very strong. These are small samples from one day, a map of what happened rather than a promise for every prompt. For an edit that comes back toned down, see the alternatives below.

Adults only in every prompt and every source photo. Do not use a real person's likeness without consent or depict anybody who could read as a minor. You are responsible for what you generate and publish. Generated media is kept for 14 days and then deleted.
